summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of incident response (DFIR) tools, books, communities, and resources for security analysts and response teams.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style link list rather than a software project. It organizes IR and digital forensics resources into about 23 sections, such as Adversary Emulation, Evidence Collection, Memory Analysis Tools, Log Analysis Tools, Timeline Tools, Playbooks, and Sandboxing/Reversing Tools. Each entry is a one-line description of a tool, book, or service, with some naming the platform it targets (Windows, Linux, macOS). Coverage spans commercial and open-source products, live-response collectors, memory acquisition and analysis frameworks, log parsers and Sigma-based detection, and incident management and SOAR platforms. The README itself does not include install steps; each linked project has its own setup.
use_cases: find a forensic tool for a specific IR task
choose a memory acquisition or analysis tool
discover DFIR books and training resources
locate Windows event log analysis tools
find incident management or case tracking software
build a timeline of a security incident
find playbooks for responding to incidents
notable: Broad coverage across the incident response lifecycle, from evidence collection to incident management and playbooks
Separate sections for Windows, Linux, and macOS evidence collection
Includes books, communities, and knowledge bases alongside tools
Flags some entries as no longer maintained, such as IOC Finder and X-Ray 2.0
caveats: Link list only; the README does not provide installable software or a single tool to run
Some listed tools are commercial, paid, or cloud-hosted (for example Belkasoft, X-Ways, CORTEX XSOAR)
Some entries are marked poorly maintained or no longer maintained
